definitionEn: one of the separate sections of a train in which passengers travel
senseNote: Выбрано британское значение «пассажирский вагон» (в американском — car); значения «карета» и «доставка груза» не рассматриваем.
situation: Looking for your seat on a long train journey, or complaining that part of the train is overcrowded.

examples.text: Our seats were in the last [[carriage]], so we had to walk the whole length of the platform.
Passengers complained that the train had only four [[carriages]] during the morning rush hour.
Could you keep your voice down? This is the quiet [[carriage]].

texts: The first-class [[carriage]] was almost empty.
We found two free seats in the next [[carriage]].
A man in our [[carriage]] was playing loud music on his phone.

badCollocation.noteRu: Грузовой вагон — goods wagon (брит.) или freight car (амер.). Carriage — вагон для пассажиров.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Тихий вагон в британском поезде — the quiet carriage. Wagon — грузовой вагон, cabinet — шкаф или правительство, chamber — зал или палата.

nuance.text: The [[carriage]] was so long that it had over sixty seats and two toilets.
nuance.explanationRu: Carriage — весь вагон целиком. Compartment — купе, небольшое закрытое отделение внутри вагона; шестидесяти мест и двух туалетов в купе не бывает.

reverse.text: We had a sleeping [[compartment]] to ourselves on the night train.
reverse.explanationRu: Отдельное купе в ночном поезде — compartment. Carriage — целый вагон, а не купе на двоих.

fixIt.text: The train was so full that I had to stand in the [[wagon]] all the way to Leeds.
fixIt.explanationRu: Пассажирский вагон в британском английском — carriage (в американском — car). Wagon — грузовой вагон, это ложный друг.

definitionEn: a company that transports passengers or goods, especially an airline
senseNote: Выбрано значение «перевозчик, авиакомпания»; значения «носитель инфекции» и «авианосец» не рассматриваем.
situation: Choosing which airline or transport company to fly or ship with, often comparing prices and service.

examples.text: Budget [[carriers]] often charge extra for seat selection and hand luggage.
The national [[carrier]] has cancelled all flights to the region because of the storm.
We switched to a cheaper [[carrier]] for our deliveries, but parcels now arrive late.

texts: Which [[carrier]] are you flying with?
The [[carrier]] lost two of our parcels last month.
The country's biggest [[carrier]] is planning to buy fifty new planes.

badCollocation.noteRu: Носильщик в отеле или на вокзале — porter. Carrier — компания-перевозчик, например авиакомпания.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Бюджетная авиакомпания — a low-cost carrier. Transporter — транспортёр (машина), conveyor — конвейер, porter — носильщик.

nuance.text: Our [[carrier]] cancelled the flight and put us on a train instead.
nuance.explanationRu: Carrier — перевозчик, крупная транспортная компания (авиакомпания). Courier — курьер, который доставляет посылки и документы; рейсы он не отменяет.

reverse.text: A [[courier]] brought the signed contract to our office by bike.
reverse.explanationRu: Человек, который привёз документы на велосипеде, — courier. Carrier — компания-перевозчик, а не курьер.

fixIt.text: Before booking, check which [[transporter]] actually operates the flight.
fixIt.explanationRu: Перевозчик, который выполняет рейс, — carrier. Transporter — машина или платформа для перевозки, а не авиакомпания.

wordFormation.text: Passengers can claim compensation from the [[carrier]] if a flight is delayed by over three hours.

reply.context: A friend asks: "Why is your flight to Rome so cheap?"
options: It's with a budget carrier — he's carrying my suitcase for free!
It's with a budget carrier, so I'm only allowed one small bag.
The carrier's pricing strategy is predicated upon ancillary revenue streams.
reply.explanationRu: Budget carrier — бюджетная авиакомпания, второй ответ естественный. В первом carrier понято как человек-носильщик, третий звучит как доклад экономиста, а не ответ другу.

definitionEn: to build a career, role or position for yourself through hard work
senseNote: Выбрано переносное значение carve out (a career, a niche) — «добиться, завоевать своим трудом», а не «вырезать из дерева».
situation: Someone works hard for years to win a special position or place for themselves in their field.

examples.text: After years of hard work, she [[carved]] out a successful career as a translator.
The small firm has [[carved]] out a niche in eco-friendly packaging.
The young striker has quickly [[carved]] out a place for himself in the national team.

texts: It takes years to [[carve]] out a reputation in this industry.
Small shops must [[carve]] out a niche to survive against online giants.
She moved to Berlin to [[carve]] out a new life for herself.

badCollocation.noteRu: Разработать план — draw up или work out a plan. Carve out — «завоевать, выкроить» себе нишу, место или карьеру.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Занять свою нишу — carve out a niche (буквально «вырезать»). Find a niche возможно, но без out; make out и take out значат совсем другое.

nuance.text: It took her ten years to [[carve]] out a name for herself in fashion.
nuance.explanationRu: Carve out a name, a niche — завоевать своим трудом. Cut out значит «вырезать ножницами» или «исключить», для карьеры не подходит.

reverse.text: I [[cut]] out the article and stuck it on the fridge.
reverse.explanationRu: Вырезать статью из газеты ножницами — cut out. Carve — резать по дереву или камню, а в переносном смысле — завоёвывать себе место.

fixIt.text: Through sheer talent, the young chef [[cut]] out a place for herself among the city's top cooks.
fixIt.explanationRu: Cut out — вырезать ножницами или исключить. Завоевать себе место своим трудом — carve out.

reply.context: At a networking event, someone asks: "How did you end up running your own design studio?"
options: I carved the studio out of wood myself, actually.
I spent ten years freelancing and slowly carved out a niche in book covers.
Yo, I just carved out, like, a niche thingy, innit.
reply.explanationRu: Carve out a niche — завоевать свою нишу, второй ответ точный. Первый понимает carve буквально (вырезать из дерева), третий слишком жаргонный для делового знакомства.

definitionEn: a person who is killed or injured in a war or an accident
senseNote: Casualties — и погибшие, и раненые, а не только погибшие.
situation: News reports say how many people were killed or hurt in a crash, flood or battle.

examples.text: The train crash caused dozens of [[casualties]], most of them with minor injuries.
The region suffered heavy [[casualties]] in the floods of 1953.
Thanks to the new speed limit, the number of [[casualties]] on the town's roads has fallen by a third.

texts: Rescue teams are still counting the [[casualties]] after the earthquake.
Hospitals were ready to receive [[casualties]] from the crash site.
Luckily, there were no [[casualties]] when the old bridge collapsed.

badCollocation.noteRu: Жертвы болезни или эпидемии — victims или deaths. Casualties — пострадавшие в войне, аварии или катастрофе.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Большие потери — heavy casualties. Big, strong и hard с casualties не сочетаются: «тяжёлые» потери по-английски именно heavy.

nuance.text: The earthquake caused heavy [[casualties]] in the old part of the city.
nuance.explanationRu: Heavy casualties — большие потери (убитые и раненые). С victims так не говорят: victim — жертва преступления, болезни или обмана.

reverse.text: She was the [[victim]] of an online scam and lost all her savings.
reverse.explanationRu: Жертва мошенничества — victim. Casualty — только убитый или раненый в войне, аварии, катастрофе.

fixIt.text: The hurricane caused many [[sacrifices]] among the island's population.
fixIt.explanationRu: «Жертвы» катастрофы — casualties (или victims). Sacrifice — жертва в смысле самопожертвования или жертвоприношения.

reply.context: Your colleague reads a headline aloud: "Bus overturns on mountain road."
options: Oh no. Was it a casualty, or did someone do it on purpose?
Pray, might one enquire as to the casualty figures?
Oh no. Were there any casualties?
reply.explanationRu: Were there any casualties? — естественный вопрос о пострадавших. В первом casualty спутано со «случайностью», второй звучит архаично и вычурно.

rewrite.original: Nobody was killed or injured in the fire.
rewrite.frame: There were no ____ in the fire.
rewrite.explanationRu: No casualties — «никто не погиб и не пострадал».

definitionEn: a long series of bad things, such as mistakes or failures
senseNote: Выбрано переносное значение «череда (ошибок, бед)», а не базовое «каталог товаров».
situation: A report or review describes one mistake or disaster after another, all in one long list.

examples.text: The official report described the hospital's response as a [[catalogue]] of errors.
Our holiday was a [[catalogue]] of disasters: lost bags, a flooded hotel and food poisoning.
The team's season has been a [[catalogue]] of injuries, defeats and bad luck.

texts: The inquiry uncovered a [[catalogue]] of failures at the company.
Her complaint letter was a long [[catalogue]] of grievances.
His career has been a [[catalogue]] of missed chances.

badCollocation.noteRu: В переносном смысле catalogue — череда неудач: a catalogue of errors, of disasters. Про победы говорят a string of victories или a run of wins.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Череда ошибок — a catalogue of errors (также series или string of errors). Menu, brochure и diary так не употребляются.

nuance.text: Critics called the new stadium project a [[catalogue]] of disasters.
nuance.explanationRu: A catalogue of disasters — образно «сплошная череда бед». List — список на бумаге; назвать сам проект «списком катастроф» по-английски нельзя.

reverse.text: Don't forget to make a shopping [[list]] before you go.
reverse.explanationRu: Список покупок — shopping list. Catalogue — каталог товаров или (перен.) череда неудач, а не записка перед походом в магазин.

fixIt.text: The builder's work was a [[row]] of costly mistakes, from leaking pipes to crooked walls.
fixIt.explanationRu: «Ряд ошибок» — не a row (ряд предметов в линию), а a catalogue of mistakes.

reply.context: A friend asks: "How was the wedding? I heard it didn't go exactly to plan."
options: It was a catalogue of disasters: the cake fell over and the band got lost.
It was lovely — the catalogue of the bride's dress was beautiful.
It was, as it were, a catalogue of unfortunate occurrences, I daresay.
reply.explanationRu: A catalogue of disasters — «сплошные неприятности», первый ответ естественный. Во втором catalogue бессмысленно, третий звучит вычурно и старомодно.

rewrite.original: The project had one serious problem after another.
rewrite.frame: The project was a ____ of serious problems.
rewrite.explanationRu: Череда проблем — a catalogue of problems.

definitionEn: to provide what a particular group of people needs or wants
senseNote: Выбрано значение cater for / cater to — «быть рассчитанным на, удовлетворять запросы»; значение «обеспечивать питание на банкете» не рассматриваем.
situation: A hotel, school or shop is designed to give a particular type of customer exactly what they need.

examples.text: The resort [[caters]] mainly for families with young children, so it's not ideal for a quiet break.
Our school [[caters]] for students with a wide range of learning needs.
Streaming services now [[cater]] to every taste, from Korean dramas to nature documentaries.

texts: The menu doesn't [[cater]] for vegetarians at all.
These courses [[cater]] to complete beginners.
Small hotels can [[cater]] for guests' individual needs.

badCollocation.noteRu: После cater нужен предлог: cater to (или for) the needs of students.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Быть рассчитанным на любой вкус — cater to (или for) every taste. Предлоги at, with и on с cater в этом значении не используются.

nuance.text: The new gym [[caters]] for older people, with gentle classes and extra-wide changing rooms.
nuance.explanationRu: Cater for — быть рассчитанным на какую-то группу: занятия и раздевалки для пожилых. Care for — лично ухаживать за больным или пожилым человеком.

reverse.text: She gave up work to [[care]] for her elderly father.
reverse.explanationRu: Ухаживать за пожилым отцом — care for. Cater for значило бы «обслуживать» или «кормить», как ресторан.

fixIt.text: The menu at the new café [[cares]] for vegans and people with food allergies.
fixIt.explanationRu: Меню не может «ухаживать» (care for) за людьми. Быть рассчитанным на веганов и аллергиков — cater for.

reply.context: A colleague asks: "Is that new hotel by the station any good for a family weekend?"
options: Not really — it caters mostly for business travellers, so there's nothing for kids.
Yes, the staff will cater for your kids at night, like babysitters.
The establishment caters, one presumes, to a clientele of a corporate nature.
reply.explanationRu: Cater for — быть рассчитанным на определённых гостей, первый ответ точный. Во втором cater спутано с care for (присматривать), третий слишком вычурный для разговора с коллегой.

rewrite.original: The magazine is written mainly for people who love gardening.
rewrite.frame: The magazine ____ people who love gardening.
rewrite.explanationRu: Быть рассчитанным на какую-то аудиторию — cater for / cater to.

definitionEn: cows and bulls that are kept on a farm for their meat or milk
senseNote: Одно значение; слово всегда во множественном числе: the cattle are grazing.
situation: A farmer moves cows from one field to another or sells them for beef.

examples.text: In summer the farmers take their [[cattle]] up to the mountains to graze.
With no grass left after the drought, the [[cattle]] had to be fed on expensive hay.
Most of the beef sold in the country comes from [[cattle]] raised on grass, not grain.

texts: Thousands of [[cattle]] died during the long, dry summer.
The [[cattle]] were grazing peacefully by the river.
The family has raised beef [[cattle]] on this land for a century.

badCollocation.noteRu: Cattle — только множественное число: many cattle, the cattle are. Одну корову называют a cow.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Herd — стадо крупных животных: a herd of cattle. У кур — flock, у волков — pack, у рыб — shoal или school.

nuance.text: The farmer sold all his [[cattle]] but kept the sheep and the chickens.
nuance.explanationRu: Cattle — только коровы и быки. Livestock — весь домашний скот, включая овец и кур, поэтому «продал весь скот, но оставил овец» звучит противоречиво.

reverse.text: The farm keeps a lot of [[livestock]]: sheep, pigs, goats and chickens.
reverse.explanationRu: Овцы, свиньи и куры — это livestock, скот вообще. Cattle — только крупный рогатый скот.

fixIt.text: The floods killed hundreds of [[cattles]] in the north of the country.
fixIt.explanationRu: Cattle уже означает множественное число и никогда не принимает -s: hundreds of cattle.

definitionEn: great care taken to avoid danger, risks or mistakes
senseNote: Значение «осторожность» в сочетаниях уровня C1: exercise caution, urge caution, err on the side of caution.
situation: Experts advise people to be very careful before making a risky decision or trusting early results.

examples.text: Experts urged [[caution]], saying the early results of the drug trial were promising but limited.
Treat any email asking for your password with extreme [[caution]].
The roads are icy this morning, so drivers should proceed with [[caution]].

texts: When in doubt, err on the side of [[caution]].
Investors are showing more [[caution]] after last year's losses.
Doctors advise [[caution]] when mixing these two medicines.

badCollocation.noteRu: С большой осторожностью — with great (или extreme) caution. Big с caution не сочетается.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Проявлять осторожность — exercise caution (или show caution). Do, make и keep с caution не сочетаются.

nuance.text: If you're not sure the mushrooms are safe, err on the side of [[caution]] and don't eat them.
nuance.explanationRu: Err on the side of caution — устойчивое выражение «лучше перестраховаться». Care в нём не используется: care — забота или аккуратность.

reverse.text: Bye, and take [[care]] on the way home!
reverse.explanationRu: Take care — «береги себя», дружеское прощание. Take caution так не говорят.

fixIt.text: Hikers are advised to exercise [[carefulness]] on the narrow mountain path after heavy rain.
fixIt.explanationRu: Со словом exercise сочетается caution: exercise caution. Carefulness — редкое слово, в таких предупреждениях его не используют.

wordFormation.text: A [[cautious]] investor would never put all her savings into one company.

rewrite.original: You should be very careful when you use this app.
rewrite.frame: This app should be used with ____.

definitionEn: careful to avoid risks, and not willing to act or decide quickly
senseNote: Значение то же, что на уровне B1; уровень C1 — в сочетаниях cautious optimism, a cautious welcome, be cautious about.
situation: Someone avoids taking risks, waits for more information and does not rush into a decision.

examples.text: After losing money in the last crash, she's become very [[cautious]] about investing.
The union gave a [[cautious]] welcome to the new pay offer, saying details still had to be agreed.
Doctors are [[cautious]] about letting him go home so soon after the operation.

texts: Scientists are [[cautious]] about drawing conclusions from one study.
The bank took a [[cautious]] approach and kept interest rates unchanged.
She's a [[cautious]] driver who never goes over the speed limit.

badCollocation.noteRu: Бытовое «Осторожно, горячо!» — Careful, it's hot! Cautious описывает человека или подход, а не предупреждение.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Сдержанно одобрить — give a cautious welcome. Careful, attentive и prudent в этом сочетании не используются.

nuance.text: The company gave a [[cautious]] estimate of five percent growth, and the real figure was much higher.
nuance.explanationRu: Cautious estimate — осторожный, заниженный «с запасом» прогноз. Careful estimate — тщательно рассчитанный; он не объясняет, почему реальность оказалась намного лучше.

reverse.text: Be [[careful]] not to spill coffee on the keyboard.
reverse.explanationRu: Be careful not to spill — бытовое «смотри не пролей». Cautious так не используется: оно о нежелании рисковать.

fixIt.text: The two leaders expressed [[careful]] optimism about the peace talks.
fixIt.explanationRu: Осторожный, сдержанный оптимизм — cautious optimism. Careful optimism так не говорят.

wordFormation.text: Analysts are [[cautiously]] optimistic about the economy next year.

reply.context: A colleague asks: "The new client wants us to start work before the contract is signed. What do you think?"
options: I'd be cautious — let's start right away and forget about the contract.
One would be well advised to adopt a cautious stance, would one not?
I'd be cautious — let's get the contract signed first.
reply.explanationRu: Cautious — не рисковать без гарантий, третий ответ логичен. Первый противоречит сам себе, второй звучит чопорно и неестественно для разговора с коллегой.

definitionEn: to stop happening, existing or doing something
situation: An official notice says that a service, company or activity will officially stop.

examples.text: The company [[ceased]] trading in 2019 after years of heavy losses.
By the end of the war, the old empire had [[ceased]] to exist.
Payments will [[cease]] if you fail to report a change in your income.

texts: The factory [[ceased]] production last spring.
Fighting finally [[ceased]] after three days of talks.
The rain [[ceased]], and the sun came out over the hills.

badCollocation.noteRu: Остановить машину — stop the car. Cease — «прекратить» деятельность или существование, а не физически остановить.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Прекратить существование — cease to exist. Stop to do значит «остановиться, чтобы что-то сделать», а finish и end с инфинитивом не употребляются.

nuance.text: His patience with difficult customers never [[ceases]] to amaze me.
nuance.explanationRu: Never ceases to amaze — «не перестаёт удивлять». Stops to amaze — ошибка: stop to do значит «остановиться, чтобы сделать»; можно never stops amazing me.

reverse.text: Could you [[stop]] tapping your pen? I'm trying to concentrate.
reverse.explanationRu: В живой речи просят stop. Cease звучит как официальный документ, в такой просьбе оно неуместно.

fixIt.text: We regret to announce that this bus service will [[quit]] on 1 March.
fixIt.explanationRu: Quit — «бросить, уволиться», о человеке. Об официальном прекращении работы сервиса — cease.

wordFormation.text: The agreement called for an immediate [[cessation]] of hostilities.

reply.context: Your landlord emails: "The noise from your flat after midnight must stop."
options: Sure, bro, the noise will totally cease, chill.
Understood. The late-night parties will cease — sorry for the trouble.
Understood. I'll cease the washing machine after midnight, then.
reply.explanationRu: Cease уместно в вежливом ответе на официальное письмо: вечеринки прекратятся. Cease the washing machine — ошибка (нужно turn off), а первый ответ слишком фамильярный.

rewrite.original: The small airline went out of business in 2020.
